lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Nadège, Kendra here. How's your Monday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the soda swap went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You should just stop buying soda.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You really enjoy that Coke.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you keep soda in the house?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My health is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to swap soda for water on 4 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the parties gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Nadège. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Kendra. Bye!

tags.note: Need to act due to cancer fear
Feels better when sticking to it
Uses fridge reminder; guilt when skipping

flags.reason: Unsolicited directive 'You should just stop buying soda' right after participant reports being fine; ignores autonomy and triggered sustain talk.
Fear-based warning 'your health is going to suffer' without permission; contradicts the autonomy stance in line 37.
Participant's kids-motivated change talk was not reinforced or explored; coach moved to 'Whatever you pick is fine' instead.

score.summary: Kendra closed with a clear, specific goal and a barrier plan, and drew out many change statements from Nadège. However, she persuaded twice (lines 8 and 38) and missed reinforcing several change statements, which undercut the collaborative tone.
strengths: Line 33 and line 50 affirm Nadège's effort and noticing of benefits.
Line 42 is a strong complex reflection that links the change to people Nadège loves.
Line 46 plans for barriers by asking about a backup plan, which led to a concrete answer at line 47.
Line 14 and line 44 invite Nadège to set her own goal.
coaching_tips: Remove the directive in line 8; ask permission first, e.g., 'Would it help to talk through options for the soda?'
Replace the fear warning in line 38 with a reflection of the stakes Nadège named, such as her grandchildren or diabetes.
When Nadège says 'My kids is why I'm doing this' (line 36), reflect it and ask her to say more rather than shifting to reassurance.
Summarize the session before closing so Nadège hears her own change talk and goal in one place.
